item.title: UNCG Trains the Team Behind the Teams
item.description: Behind every athletic team is a team of coaches, advisors, trainers, and physicians who keep them healthy and motivated. Learn more about the UNCG programs developing workforce-ready graduates and research to improve the experience of athletes at all levels.

item.title: AI@Work in Nursing
item.description: UNCG’s School of Nursing integrates AI into coursework, simulation and faculty training to enhance learning and prepare future nurses.

item.title: Health Expo Tour Makes a Stop at UNCG
item.description: The Health Professions Graduate School Fair is part of the North Carolina Health Career Expo Tour. It will present 75 programs from various health fields on March 25. Students of all majors are welcome to come by and learn more about potential educational and career pathways for after they graduate.

item.title: Undergrad Researcher Maps New Pathways in Bone Biology at UNCG
item.description: A UNCG senior majoring in biology with a minor in chemistry, Jonah has spent the last three semesters developing an innovative method to analyze the microstructural growth of thigh bones of individuals aged 3 months to 18 years.

item.title: The Early History of Women’s Athletics At the G, 1892-1950
item.description: University Archivist Dr. Erin Lawrimore has chronicled UNCG’s legacy of women’s athletics in Power Point presentations, PDFs, and the Spartan Stories blog. She pored over old photos and documents to piece this history together.

item.description: Before seniors Ava Hall and Cameron Dupree graduate in May, they’ll have accomplished a significant feat. The two presented at the Honors Symposium sponsored by UNC Greensboro's Lloyd International Honors College on March 20.

item.description: In the performances and panels this month, UNCG faculty will lead discussions on building trust across language, how we perceive AI, and share a month-long art exhibition of work combining different disciplines in creative practice.

item.title: Spartans Thrive Engagement Grants Foster Student Wellness and Innovation Across Campus
item.description: The Spartans Thrive initiative awarded grants to three proposals that will support students in a holistic way. The three awardees will work on student-to-student mentorship, connecting them to healthy activities, and fostering leadership skills with the help of nationally recognized workshops.

item.title: Chef Aarti’s Party Comes to UNCG
item.description: Chef Aarti Sequeira brought her party to UNCG to teach students how to make chutney and judge Spartan Dining’s Spring 2026 Battle of the Chefs.

item.title: Science Everywhere Festival creates fun for all ages on UNCG Campus
item.description: Join us for the Science Everywhere Festival at UNCG on Saturday, April 11, 2026, from noon to 4 p.m. The event, which is free and open to all ages, features over 50 stations of interactive experiments, tours of science research labs, presentations by student and faculty scientists, a cardboard robot parade, food trucks, and more.

item.title: Johnson Alumni House Opens Reservations
item.description: The Marcus T. Johnson Alumni House is now taking spring reservations. Anyone wishing to use one of its spaces to host an event or meeting can set a date with Advancement.
